newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Palm oil seen raising share in oils and fats trade.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil seen raising share in oils and fats trade.

text.p: Palm oil will increase its share in the world trade in oils and fats to 43.6 percent by 2000 from 35.7 percent in 1995, an official of Malaysia's Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) said on Thursday.

"The recent trend shows that in terms of proportion of world production and trade of oils and fats, there has been a marked shift from soya oil and animal fats to palm oil," PORLA's Mamat Bin Salleh said at the Asian Oilseeds conference in Singapore.

Ahmad Ibrahim, director of marketing and promotion for the Malaysia Palm Oil Promotion Council (MPOPC), said a total of 15.3 million tonnes of palm oil was produced in 1995. Malaysia accounted for 53 percent of the total and Indonesia 21 percent.
While lagging behind soya oil, whose total world output last year reached 20.2 million tonnes, palm was the leading oil traded in the world, Ahmad said.

Some 10.5 million tonnes of palm oil was traded in the world's markets last year representing nearly 36 percent of the total traded. Soya oil accounted for about 19.0 percent of trades in the oils and fats market.
Mamat estimates that palm oil production will rise to 31.63 million tonnes by 2000 to roughly equal the output of soya oil. By 2005, palm output will hit 35.03 million tonnes.
World production of oils and fats in 2000 will probably reach 108.28 million tonnes and 123 million tonnes in 2005.
"The proportion of the world trade for palm oil (will rise to) 43.6 percent as compared to 14.1 percent for soya oil," Mamat said.
But Ahmad said palm will have to contend with tariff and non-tariff barriers in major markets like China and India, which buys about one million tonnes of palm oil each.

"There is still a lot of convincing to do before palm oil can enjoy parity tariffs as with other oils. When that happens, palm oil is set to dominate an even bigger share of the world market for oils and fats," Ahmad said.
